label: Fish position (derived)
_note: A derived fish-position state. No registry lake has a live thermocline or dissolved-oxygen sensor, so the state is inferred from what the engine already knows: the lake's mixing type (config/lakes.json) plus modeled surface water temperature, month, existing lake state, and spawn phase. While `stratified` is active, presentation classes get a small T5 tie-break translation (kb/CONDITIONS.md): suspended presentations stay in the oxygenated layer above the stratification level. While `overwinter` is active, the deep-water cold-feed translation leads with bottom-oriented presentations. A trigger with no `mixing_any` is temperature-driven, not stratification-driven, and fires for any water (winter). Spring staging is owned by the spawn phase (kb/spawn.json), so it is not duplicated here. Null-safe: unknown mixing type or water temp means no state, no fit.

provenance.author: position-pass/1.1
provenance.note: trigger facts are T2 verbatim; class-fit directions are T2-anchored where quotes exist, magnitudes are T5 editorial translations on the capped tie-break layer

state_notes.stratified: bass hold above the stratification level — “There is no oxygen or fish below the stratification level” (Iowa DNR)
state_notes.overwinter: bass have returned to deep water as the lake cooled through the low-to-mid 50s, and feeding is greatly reduced below 50°F (Iowa DNR)

suspend.note: holds in the oxygenated layer above the stratification level

fall.note: slow fall stays in the oxygenated layer

bottom.note: deep, slow drag on the bottom — winter bass move slowly along the bottom (Take Me Fishing) and the cold-water feed is reduced

suspend.note: a bait held above the bottom in the deep water column — some winter bass suspend

citations.claim: summer position is set by temperature and dissolved oxygen; no fish below the stratification level
citations.quote: Along with temperature, dissolved oxygen is a major factor determining where to find bass during summer. Many Iowa lakes stratify at depths from 6 to 20 feet. There is no oxygen or fish below the stratification level.

citations.claim: summer bass seek 77–80°F and avoid water over 80°F
citations.quote: Most bass avoid water that exceeds 80 degrees and seek 77 to 80 degrees places.

citations.claim: drop shot presents a bait to suspended bass above the bottom
citations.source: Take Me Fishing — Bass Fishing Rigs
citations.quote: Drop shot rigs are also popular bass fishing rigs as they allow you to present a soft plastic lure above the bottom to bass that are suspended just above the bottom.

citations.claim: as the water cools through the low-to-mid 50s, bass return to deep water
citations.quote: As fall progresses and water temperature cools to the low to mid-50's, bass will return to deep waters.

citations.claim: feeding is greatly reduced below 50°F (cold-water fish are slow)
citations.quote: Bass feeding is greatly reduced below 50 degrees as they become tired.

citations.claim: winter bass feed slowly and along the bottom (Texas/Carolina soft plastics)
citations.source: Take Me Fishing — Want 4 Tips on How to Catch Bass in the Winter? (Dec 2022)
citations.quote: Use soft plastic baits or lures (such as Texas-rigged or Carolina-rigged worms) that move slowly along the bottom instead.

citations.claim: cold-water finesse keeps contact with the bottom and moves in slow hops
citations.source: Take Me Fishing — Cold Water Bass Fishing (Dec 2016)
citations.quote: Finesse. Switch to lighter line and try a small jig at the front of a 6-inch rubber worm. Try to keep in contact with the bottom and give it slow, little hops.

citations.claim: some winter bass suspend and take small presentations in front of them
citations.source: Take Me Fishing — Want 4 Tips on How to Catch Bass in the Winter? (Dec 2022)
citations.quote: Bass may be suspended during this time of year and prefer to “snack” on smaller, more convenient prey items that are presented right in front of them.
